title: The month of Phagun
hook: in Phagun bliss comes, the Friend revealed (Barah Maha, ang 136)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the month of Magh, and your line: magh: humble bath. Did you take one low place on purpose? Washed of pride, the bride reaches the last month of the year. Day five hundred seventy-seven.
screen: `THE MONTH OF MAGH — MAGH: HUMBLE BATH.`

segments.voice: There's a particular sound at an airport arrivals gate. Someone has been waiting a long time, checking the board, rereading the same text. Then the doors slide open, and they see the face. The sound they make isn't a word. It's half a laugh and half a cry, and everybody nearby turns and smiles. Phagun, roughly mid-February to mid-March, is when Punjab's winter breaks. Mustard is in flower, the days warm, and in the Barah Maha, after eleven months of longing, the doors finally open.
screen: `THE ARRIVALS GATE.` → `HALF A LAUGH, HALF A CRY.` → `PHAGUN: THE DOORS OPEN.`

segments.voice: The stanza opens phalgun anand upaarjanaa, har sajan pragate aa-e. In paraphrase: in Phagun, bliss springs up; the Lord, the Friend, has appeared. Anand is bliss, deep joy, the same word that names Guru Amar Das's hymn Anand Sahib. Upaarjanaa is to arise, to be produced. And sajan is a friend, a dear one, the word you'd use for someone you love. Pragate aa-e: has come, made visible. So after all those months of the Beloved being far, here He is, revealed. Notice who brings it about. The saints, the Lord's helpers, the stanza says, in their kindness have brought about the meeting. That's the holy company we met in Assu and Maghar, still at work. Then the stanza fills with celebration. The bed is beautiful, every comfort is here, and now there's no room for sorrow. Her wish is fulfilled. Friends gather and sing songs of joy, the songs of the Lord of the world. And then a quiet line: no one else like the Lord can be seen; there's no other to compare with Him. Phagun is the season of spring festivals. Holi falls near its end, and the day after, Sikhs gather at Anandpur Sahib for Hola Mohalla, begun by Guru Gobind Singh. Color, music, a crowd. The Barah Maha's bliss isn't private. It's a party with friends. And there's a lesson in the order. Bliss doesn't come first in the year. It comes last, after doubt, longing, honesty and humility. The stanza doesn't say those months were wasted. It says they led here.
screen: `ANAND: BLISS SPRINGS UP.` · `SAJAN: THE FRIEND, REVEALED.` · `THE SAINTS BRING THE MEETING.` · `FRIENDS GATHER AND SING.` · then, large: `PHAGUN: BLISS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: celebrate one small thing. Sit comfortably and look back over the last few days. Find one thing that went right, however small: a warm call, a good meal, a task finished, a moment of laughter. Let yourself actually enjoy it again, not just note it. Smile if you like. Then think who you could tell, because Phagun's joy is shared. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru between breaths, or hum a line of a shabad you love. The bell holds the time.
The month of Phagun. In the Barah Maha, Phagun is the last month of the year and the month of meeting: bliss springs up, and the Friend is revealed.
Your line: phagun: bliss. Today, tell one person about one good thing, and let them be glad with you. Joy grows when it's shared. Day five hundred seventy-seven.

howItsDone: On the Sangrand of Phagun many gurdwaras read the Phagun stanza of Guru Arjan's Barah Maha; around the same season Sikhs gather at Anandpur Sahib for Hola Mohalla, begun by Guru Gobind Singh.

fork.setup: after eleven months of longing, the Friend appears in Phagun. what does the bride do?
options: keep it quiet in case it doesn't last.
gather friends and sing songs of joy.
fork.reveal: the stanza fills with celebration: friends gather and sing songs of the Lord of the world. Phagun's bliss is shared.

original.note: Gurmukhi: anand, bliss. The same word names Guru Amar Das's Anand Sahib and the city of Anandpur.

trapdoor: what you thought: Phagun is about spring weather.
what it means: it's the month the long separation ends, and the Friend is revealed with shared joy.
what a scholar hears: Guru Arjan's twelve months run from Chet to Phagun, the order of the Indian year, so union arrives in the year's last month, after the whole cycle of longing.

sources.ref: Barah Maha, Raag Majh, Mahalla 5, the Phagun stanza (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 136)
